name: GWF Interbrand Championship
epitaph: The only reign the surviving record recovers for the GWF Interbrand Championship is The Reprobate's own eight-month run, closing 22 March 2009 — who he won it from, and who took it from him, went uncaptured.

name: GWF Championship
epitaph: GWF's own top prize, worn by Wolfenstein as the fed's first Undisputed Champion in its earliest days, then by James Murphy, then Michael Toaster, then Chris O'Malley after Locked N' Loaded 2007, then SheltonSplash after Valentine's Vengeance 2008, then Don Cicinni after three Omerta superkicks in a match recovered only as a flashback. The belt's own last night is the fed's own last night: on 20 January 2013's closing show, "20113," Chris O'Malley pinned Robert Garland in a four-way lumberjack match to become GWF's final champion — the title, like the promotion around it, going dark undefeated.
notes: "GWF Global Championship" is the name a single flashback promo gives the belt Don Cicinni won from SheltonSplash (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html); every other surviving reference calls it the GWF Championship or GWF World Championship. Recorded as one title under the more common name rather than split, per THE REBIRTH DOCTRINE's own default-to-one-record posture, absent evidence of two distinct belts.

name: GWF Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: Chris O'Malley's own long-held prize — he defended it as recently as 2013's reunion-tour build — forfeited voluntarily at 20113 in exchange for a slot in the closing show's own GWF Championship match. Five men (SheltonSplash, Ken Davidson, Nitro Nick, Jeff Maximus and Chris Williams) fought to fill the vacancy that same night in a five-way elimination match; Chris Williams outlasted them all to become the belt's own final champion.

name: GWF United States Championship
epitaph: Crowned in an eight-man reunion-tour tournament on 27 March 2009, the United States title went to Star-Man, the field's own least-experienced entrant, over The Reprobate in the final. Star-Man held it through the fed's own last night, retaining against Reprobate one final time at 20113 in January 2013.

name: GWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A well-traveled belt: SheltonSplash and Kevin McAuliffe lost it to XO Malone and Damian DeNiro's own Movement in a match the record keeps only as a flashback; by April 2008 The Number 4 and Michael Toaster's own Numbered Toast held it, walking out on their own title defense at that month's War Games rather than lose it clean; by 2013 it belonged to Dave Shadow and Kevin McAuliffe's own Neo-Evolution, who lost it in the fed's own last hours to Danny Mainer and Bryan Daniels — the final GWF Tag Team Champions.
notes: The Billionaires Club (Wolfenstein and John Beanshaw Wrathfield)'s own reign, named only in a 28 July 2008 Hall of Shame retrospective with no result or date recovered, likely precedes all five dated/flashback reigns above; recorded on this same title id rather than split, given no evidence of a distinct belt.

name: GWF International Xtreme Championship
epitaph: Falcon McKenzie retained it against Michael Smart in a bloody hardcore defense on 27 April 2008; by the 2009 reunion tour it belonged to Baron Trotter, who fended off a returning Mark Madison in a billed-but-uncaptured defense and carried it to the fed's own last night. At 20113, Baron unified it with the Co-Cruiserweight Championship in a triple threat against XO Malone and Debolt Dragonsbane, becoming the Undisputed GWF International Xtreme Champion for GWF's own final record.

name: GWF Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Lodis3 held it three times in GWF's earliest days, per the fed's own Hall of Shame retrospective. The Reprobate's own March 2009 bio card lists a further, undated reign already ended by that point. By the January 2013 closing show the belt sat vacant after holder Jay Ramirez's arrest, until SheltonSplash handed it back to Reprobate backstage and made his very next tournament bout a title defense — which Reprobate won, retaining the belt through the fed's own last night.

name: GWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Toast Hogan's own belt during the 2006 Food Division craze the fed's own Hall of Shame remembers fondly. Retired by Alex Storm ahead of the 2013 closing show and fought for one last time between Debolt Dragonsbane and XO Malone, a match Baron Trotter interrupted before either man could win it outright — Storm declared the two Co-Champions on the spot. The lineage ended that same night, unified into the International Xtreme Championship.
notes: Toast Hogan is Michael Toaster's own retired early gimmick (see michael-toaster's tenure); his 2006 reign is remembered only in retrospective, no date or result recovered.

events.title: gwf-2006-international-xtreme
events.note: Baron Trotter's win over the Co-Champions in a triple threat for the "Undisputed GWF International Xtreme Championship" folded this lineage into that title.

name: GWF Breakthrough Championship
epitaph: A brand-new belt minted for one night only: the closing show's own single-elimination Breakthrough Tournament, its winner promised a GWF Championship match in the same evening's main event. Robert "Badger" Garland outlasted Chris Williams in the final to become the only man ever to hold it.
notes: `nature: self-awarded` reflects that this belt was created and awarded within a single night's own tournament rather than defended on any ordinary schedule, not that it was uncontested — eight men fought across two rounds and a final for it.

name: Sunday Brunch Heavyweight-Interbrand Championship
epitaph: A title of GWF's own lower-card Brunch program, distinct from the main-roster Interbrand Championship despite the shared name. Michael Smart held it into the fed's own last night, entering the closing show's Champion of Champions match on the strength of it.
notes: No won-date or prior result survives — Michael Smart names himself the holder from the ring at 20113, on a technicality, to force his own way into the Champion of Champions match.

name: GWF Champion of Champions
epitaph: A one-night-only elimination gauntlet at the fed's own closing show, open to every titleholder in the building. Michael Smart, entering on a technicality with a lower-card belt few in the room even remembered, outlasted them all to become GWF's only Champion of Champions.
